summary: What's the procedure for updating existing worker nodes created by `eksctl`? This is obviously not the same template that `eksctl` uses. Should this be done using `eksctl` somehow, or should we be updating the CloudFormation stack that `eksctl` creates? Assume I've already upgraded my cluster (i.e. from 1.10 to 1.11) and I've replaced `kube-dns` with CoreDN
title: [EKS]: How to upgrade worker nodes created by eksctl?

This will allow customers to move fast by avoiding maintaining kops based kubernetes deployments when deploying to regions that you are currently not supporting.
title: [EKS] [Global Rollout]: Deploy to all remaining AWS Regions

summary: AWS EKS provides us a great comfort managing the control plain for our kubernetes cluster but at the same time, it is forcing us to make a frequent upgrade on kubernetes version. This may not be ideal for critical production clusters. If you see kubernetes 1.16 it got a lot of breaking changes and not compatible with previous k8s api's. I'm asking the EKS team to consider LTS version on EKS/Kubernetes for customers to be on a version for at least 1 year. LTS version is a standard practice and it prevents developer cycle doing multiple upgrades every few months for a feature we don't need/want.
title: EKS : Consider LTS versions on EKS
